reasoning: This is the classic Pigeonhole Principle problem. We have 11 pigeons that must each be assigned to exactly one of 10 holes, with each hole containing at most one pigeon. Since there are more pigeons (11) than holes (10), and each hole can hold at most one pigeon, it is mathematically impossible to assign all 11 pigeons without placing at least two pigeons in the same hole. Therefore, this problem is UNSATISFIABLE.
